description: When a commander would go to the graveyard, its owner may choose to move it to the command zone instead (the 'commander replacement effect'), and the commander tax increases by {2} for each time it has been cast from the command zone, applying on its next cast from there.
artificial_state_elements: Lethal combat damage killing Tymna is an arbitrary trigger for the death event - any effect that would put the commander into the graveyard from the battlefield works identically.
The opposing attacker's identity/power is not material, only that it deals lethal damage.
material_characteristics: The commander replacement effect is optional per-instance, applied by the owner as the permanent would move to the graveyard (CR 903.9a) - it is not automatic
Commander tax: {2} more to cast for each previous time it was cast from the command zone this game (CR 903.8), tracked cumulatively regardless of zone changes in between
abstracted_characteristics: The specific source of lethal damage/destruction - any would-be graveyard-bound death event triggers the same choice
All board state not directly involved in the death and recast

legal_actions: As Tymna the Weaver would be put into the graveyard from the battlefield, its owner may choose to move it to the command zone instead (commander replacement effect)
illegal_actions_to_reject: Treating the move to the command zone as mandatory (it is a choice the owner makes each time) or as free of the accumulated commander tax on its next cast
expected.outcome_if_resolved: Owner chooses the replacement effect: Tymna moves to the command zone instead of the graveyard. On its next cast from the command zone, its cost is {2} more than the previous time it was cast from there (cumulative commander tax, CR 903.8).

engine_cross_check.notes: sim/rules_engine/xmage_tests/TymnaThrasiosCommanderSequencingTest.java, testLandDropThenFirstCastsNoTaxThenDeathAndTaxedRecast, 1/1 passing, run 2026-08-12 against a from-source XMage build (JDK 21). That test exercises this exact mechanism on Thrasios, Triton Hero rather than Tymna (Doom Blade's target selection in the test harness landed on Thrasios, empirically and repeatably, not Tymna as originally scripted) - CR 903.8/903.9 apply identically to either commander, so this fixture's claim (illustrated here with Tymna) is the one actually engine-verified, just via the other commander of the pair.
